content: If you or someone else has accidentally taken too much linezolid, seek medical attention immediately. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222 for assistance. If you miss a dose of linezolid, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. It is crucial to complete the entire prescribed course of linezolid, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to linezolid or similar antibiotics. Linezolid, commonly known by the brand name Zyvox, is an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by specific bacteria, including pneumonia, skin infections, and certain antibiotic-resistant infections. However, its appropriateness depends on the type of bacteria causing the infection, as some bacteria may have developed resistance to linezolid. Your healthcare provider may also prescribe linezolid for other conditions as deemed necessary. Linezolid works by inhibiting the growth of certain bacteria by preventing them from producing essential proteins. Linezolid is available in the following forms: 600 mg oral tablets, 100 mg/5 mL oral suspension, and injectable formulations. Oral tablets and liquid forms of linezolid should be stored at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). Store the medication in a cool, dry place, in a tightly closed container, and protect it from light. For the oral liquid, do not shake the bottle. Instead, turn it upside down 3 to 5 times before measuring each dose. Use an accurate measuring device, as household spoons may lead to incorrect dosing. Consult your pharmacist for a suitable measuring device. Common side effects of linezolid include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, headache, and anemia. If these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here, so contact your healthcare provider if you suspect any adverse reactions. Serious side effects of linezolid include: 1. Severe Allergic Reactions: Stop using linezolid and seek immediate medical help if you experience breathing difficulties, wheezing, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, throat tightness, itching, skin rash, or hives. 2. Decreased Blood Cell Production (Myelosuppression): Linezolid may reduce blood cell production in the bone marrow. Attend all scheduled blood tests to monitor this condition. 3. Serotonin Syndrome: Linezolid can increase serotonin levels in the body, which may lead to serotonin syndrome when combined with certain medications. Symptoms include confusion, agitation, headache, fever, sweating, abnormal heartbeat, muscle twitching, stiffness, shivering, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Seek emergency help if these symptoms occur. 4. Nerve Damage (Peripheral Neuropathy): Linezolid may cause damage to peripheral nerves or the optic nerve, leading to vision changes, pain, burning, tingling, numbness, or weakness in the arms, hands, legs, or feet. Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms develop. 5. Seizures: Some individuals taking linezolid have reported seizures. Symptoms may include muscle twitching, jerking, spasms, tremors, stiffening of the arms and legs, anxiety, confusion, dizziness, or loss of consciousness. Stop taking linezolid and contact your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. 6. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) in the gut can occur with antibiotics like linezolid, even up to two months after stopping the medication. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, severe stomach cramps, or fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms occur. 7. Low Sodium Levels (Hyponatremia): Linezolid may cause dangerously low sodium levels, which can be life-threatening. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, confusion, memory problems, weakness, tiredness, breathing difficulties, muscle cramps, seizures, or balance issues. Your healthcare provider may monitor your sodium levels. 8. High Lactic Acid Levels (Lactic Acidosis): Linezolid may lead to a buildup of lactic acid in the blood. Symptoms include rapid breathing, abnormal heartbeat, vomiting, extreme fatigue, or muscle weakness. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. Linezolid should not be used by individuals allergic to linezolid, Zyvox, or any ingredients in the product. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking to avoid potential drug interactions. Linezolid should not be taken with certain medications, including cold remedies containing pseudoephedrine, SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, tricyclic antidepressants, triptans, buspirone, opioids, or diabetes medications. Avoid consuming large amounts of foods or drinks high in tyramine, such as aged cheeses, sauerkraut, pickled foods, tap beer, soy sauce, red wine, and smoked meats, while taking linezolid. It is unclear if alcohol consumption affects linezolid. Do not take linezolid unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Take it exactly as directed and do not share it with others, even if they have similar symptoms. Keep linezolid out of reach of children. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your healthcare provider, as the effects of linezolid on pregnancy and breastfeeding are not fully known.
